inheritance|is-a|extends: One class extends another; "Car is a type of Vehicle, inheriting its properties and methods" (slides 7, 9). See [Inheritance is is-a, composition is has-a](#/comp4537-l1/oop-in-javascript).
composition|has-a: Build a class from separate classes; "Car has an Engine as a component"; "The composition approach allows more flexibility" (slides 8, 9). See [Inheritance is is-a, composition is has-a](#/comp4537-l1/oop-in-javascript).
super: The call in a subclass constructor, `super(brand)`, that runs the parent class's constructor (slide 7; the slide asks "What does 'super' do?"). See [Inheritance is is-a, composition is has-a](#/comp4537-l1/oop-in-javascript).
template string|string interpolation|bac: "Automatic replacing of variables with real values is called string interpolation", written with backtick ( ` ) characters (slide 8). See [Inheritance is is-a, composition is has-a](#/comp4537-l1/oop-in-javascript).
separation of concerns: "each function is responsible to deliver one single simple task, not more" (slides 164, 165). See [const first, never var, and no hard-coded user-facing strings](#/comp4537-l1/coding-style).
hard-coded string|user-facing string: A message shown to users written directly in code; "Absolutely no hard coded user facing string messages anywhere in your assignment code" (slide 16). See [const first, never var, and no hard-coded user-facing strings](#/comp4537-l1/coding-style).
shared hosting: Your site sits on a server with hundreds of others "sharing resources such as memory, disk space, CPU"; cheapest, may be slowest (slide 22). See [DevTools, the four kinds of hosting, and index.html](#/comp4537-l1/devtools-and-hosting).
VPS|virtual private server: Shares a server with other sites but "you get your own virtual private server", fewer sites, likely faster (slide 22). See [DevTools, the four kinds of hosting, and index.html](#/comp4537-l1/devtools-and-hosting).
dedicated server: "a single physical machine dedicated to your website" (slide 23). See [DevTools, the four kinds of hosting, and index.html](#/comp4537-l1/devtools-and-hosting).
cloud hosting: "multiple machines to act as one system" to handle high traffic or spikes (slide 23). See [DevTools, the four kinds of hosting, and index.html](#/comp4537-l1/devtools-and-hosting).
SSL|HTTPS: The certificate that lets you "host https:// instead of only http://"; "HTTPS stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (it uses separate protocols called SSL)" (slides 21, 44). See [DevTools, the four kinds of hosting, and index.html](#/comp4537-l1/devtools-and-hosting).
DOM|Document Object Model: The tree the browser forms in memory for a page; "How those elements are logically attached to each other is determined by a tree graph called DOM" (slides 36, 38, 152). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
element:
The building block of a page: an opening tag, content and a closing tag, e.g. `

Hello world!

` (slide 39). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
attribute: "used to provide additional information about HTML elements", e.g. `href`, `src`, `alt` (slides 40, 41). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
empty tag|single tag|void element:
A tag with nothing between open and close, such as `
`, ``, `
` (slides 39, 48). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
id: A global attribute whose "value has to be unique"; only one element per page with the same id (slide 75). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
class: A global attribute whose value "does not have to be unique" (slide 76). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
URL|Uniform Resource Locator: "a four-part addressing scheme": protocol, domain name, folder pathname, file name (slide 45). See [HTML elements, attributes and the DOM tree](#/comp4537-l1/html-structure).
inline styling: "Styling HTML elements using the style attribute" (slide 68). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
internal styling: "Using <style> tags in the <head> section of same HTML file" (slide 68). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
external styling: "Using an external CSS file", linked with `<link rel="stylesheet">`; the file "should not contain any html tags" (slides 68, 173). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
rule-set|declaration block: "A CSS rule-set consists of a selector and a declaration block"; each declaration is a property name : value pair (slide 78). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
selector: "points to the HTML element you want to style"; finds elements by name, id, class, attribute (slides 78, 80). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
descendant selector|combinator:
`div p` "selects all

elements inside

elements"; others are child (>), adjacent sibling (+), general sibling (~) (slide 185). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
specificity: The rules the browser follows to decide which of "two or more conflicting CSS rules" is most specific "and therefore wins out" (slide 186). See [Inline, internal and external styles, selectors and specificity](#/comp4537-l1/css-selectors-and-specificity).
box model: "A box that wraps around HTML element": content, padding, border, margin (slide 177). See [Content, padding, border, margin; display, position and units](#/comp4537-l1/css-box-model-display-position).
padding: "Clears an area around the content. The padding is transparent" (slide 177). See [Content, padding, border, margin; display, position and units](#/comp4537-l1/css-box-model-display-position).
margin: "Clears an area outside the border. The margin is transparent" (slide 177). See [Content, padding, border, margin; display, position and units](#/comp4537-l1/css-box-model-display-position).
block-level element: "always starts on a new line and takes up the full width available" (slide 180). See [Content, padding, border, margin; display, position and units](#/comp4537-l1/css-box-model-display-position).
inline element: "does not start on a new line and only takes up as much width as necessary" (slide 180). See [Content, padding, border, margin; display, position and units](#/comp4537-l1/css-box-model-display-position).
primitive: One of the six non-object types in ECMA6: Boolean, null, undefined, Number, String, Symbol (slide 113). See [Four ways to output, six primitives, == vs ===](#/comp4537-l1/js-values-and-types).
falsy: "undefined, null, 0, false, NaN, '' (empty string) are all falsy", meaning false in an if condition (slide 114). See [Four ways to output, six primitives, == vs ===](#/comp4537-l1/js-values-and-types).
block scope|block-scoped: Visible only within the block, "lines of codes within {}"; how `let` and `const` declare (slides 115, 127). See [var is function-scoped and hoisted; let and const are block-scoped](#/comp4537-l1/scope-and-hoisting).
function scope|function-scoped: Visible in the whole function it was declared in; how `var` declares (slides 115, 127). See [var is function-scoped and hoisted; let and const are block-scoped](#/comp4537-l1/scope-and-hoisting).
hoisting: The engine "treats all variable declarations using "var" as if they are declared at the top of a functional scope" (slide 132). See [var is function-scoped and hoisted; let and const are block-scoped](#/comp4537-l1/scope-and-hoisting).
parameter|argument: The parameter is the name in the definition (`name`); the argument is the "actual value" passed (`'John'`) (slide 163). See [Every function returns something, at least undefined](#/comp4537-l1/functions-and-arrows).
arrow function: The ES6 short form `(a,b) => a+b`; one parameter may drop the parentheses (slide 168). See [Every function returns something, at least undefined](#/comp4537-l1/functions-and-arrows).
object constructor: A function called with `new` that sets properties with `this`; "the same as function declaration" (slide 142). See [Objects, constructors and building the DOM from JavaScript](#/comp4537-l1/objects-and-the-dom).
event handler: Code run when "things" happen to HTML elements; inline (`onclick="…"`) or in a JavaScript block (slides 136, 137). See [Objects, constructors and building the DOM from JavaScript](#/comp4537-l1/objects-and-the-dom).
event queue: Where a `setTimeout` callback waits until the script finishes; why the script prints 1 3 2 even with 0 ms (slide 162). See [setTimeout runs after the script, even with 0 ms](#/comp4537-l1/timers-and-the-event-queue).
